name: The Queers
label: Lookout!
lede: Joe King kept writing Ramones songs for forty years. A drunk but well-rehearsed two days in Indiana gave him the best-selling record of the bunch, and a fight over an Epitaph deal cost him his rhythm section.

eras.title: A basement in Portsmouth
eras.text: Joe King, Scott Gildersleeve and Jack Hayes cover the Ramones in a New Hampshire basement. A second lineup plays about six shows before it ends in 1984, and the name and the songs stay.

years.h: Rehearsing Dave Clark Five songs in Tulu's basement
years.p: Joe King (Joe Queer), Scott Gildersleeve (Tulu) and Jack Hayes (Wimpy Rutherford) start the Queers in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. They cover the Monkees and the [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]] too, and never play a gig.
years.xp: Wikipedia's account has Tulu introducing the others to the Ramones in 1976. King had also spent time in Manhattan Beach, California, seeing LA punk bands including [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] and the Germs, and came home fired up.

years.h: Tulu writes "We'd Have a Riot Doing Heroin" in about two minutes
years.p: After hearing Black Flag's TV Party and the Angry Samoans' The Queer Pills, the band starts writing its own songs, and this is the first.
years.xp: Tulu has said the name means strange or an outsider, not sexual orientation.

years.h: Keith Hages joins on bass and the band plays about six shows
years.p: The gigs are in Portsmouth and Portland, Maine, and it ends in late 1984. The Love Me and Kicked Out of the Webelos EPs come from this stretch.

eras.title: Joe tries again
eras.text: King rebuilds with new players and keeps going until 1989, when he buys a restaurant.

years.h: Joe King starts over with Hugh O'Neill on drums
years.p: J.J. Rassler joins on guitar and Kevin Kecy on bass. O'Neill stays on drums for most of the next decade.

years.h: A restaurant ends the 1985 lineup
years.p: King buys one instead of making a record, per Wikipedia. The retirement is short: the band is back in 1990.

eras.title: Lookout! signs the band Ben Weasel vouched for
eras.text: With Hugh O'Neill and new bassist B-Face, King makes Grow Up, Ben Weasel champions it, and Larry Livermore signs the band to Lookout!, where the best-known records come out.

years.h: King rebuilds again with O'Neill and B-Face
years.p: Bassist B-Face (Chris Barnard) and rhythm guitarist Sean Rowley join, and Rowley leaves for art school the same year.

years.h: Grow Up gets the band noticed around New England
years.p: Shakin' Street Records puts out the debut. Screeching Weasel's [[Ben Weasel|bdce6736-8bc6-4818-8fd7-781822b674a9]] hears it and starts championing the band.

years.h: Larry Livermore sums up the Queers
years.p: Livermore, who runs Lookout!, gets King's demo through Ben Weasel around 1991 and hears doo-wop and Beach Boys melodies under the Ramones buzz.
years.xp: Wikipedia has the line as Livermore's description of the band. He signs them, and the Lookout! years run from there to 1996.

years.big: "A bleary-eyed band surrounded by a staggering array of bottles."
years.src: Wikipedia: Love Songs for the Retarded
years.h: Two days at Sonic Iguana in Lafayette, Indiana
years.p: [[Mass Giorgini|abcbcb2a-f783-4300-ba85-3cb1a32c6b2b]] engineers on November 7 and 8, 1992, and Ben Weasel produces. Most of the songs for Love Songs for the Retarded are done in one or two takes.
years.xp: That's Livermore on the album cover photo, and his guess at what the session looked like. The band was drunk but had rehearsed, Weasel kept things focused, and Giorgini worked methodically.

years.src: Wikipedia: Love Songs for the Retarded
years.h: Love Songs for the Retarded comes out on Lookout!
years.p: April 13. It becomes the band's best seller, past 100,000 copies according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: Reviewer Kembrew McLeod calls it "a giant leap from their first album." Robert Christgau gives it an honorable mention. After the band takes its masters back from Lookout!, Asian Man reissues it in 2007, remixed and remastered by Giorgini, and Rad Girlfriend does another edition in 2017.

years.h: Shout at the Queers is cut with a fill-in drummer
years.p: Jay Adelberg fills in on drums because Hugh O'Neill is out. Livermore recalls heroin hitting both O'Neill and King, and the band stages an intervention.
years.xp: King, Livermore says, managed to stop drinking, but the heroin affected both King and O'Neill. The intervention forces O'Neill to take a leave of absence.

years.h: On the road with Screeching Weasel and Rancid
years.p: The tour behind Love Songs pairs the Queers with two of the busiest bands on the Lookout! and Epitaph circuit. The clip is Maxwell's in Hoboken, spring 1994.

years.h: Beat Off is recorded in a week at Flat Iron Studios, Chicago
years.p: Ben Weasel produces April 1 to 7, and Screeching Weasel's Dan Panic plays drums while O'Neill is out with addiction.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Dan Vapid's guitar and backing vocals were removed from the final mix by Weasel. Vapid says he only learned this when royalties never came. Weasel wanted a no-frills sound, while King and Livermore wanted fuller arrangements, which led to the Surf Goddess EP later that summer.

years.h: The Queers play the Ramones' Rocket to Russia start to finish
years.p: Jay Adelberg drums on the complete re-recording of the band's biggest influence.

years.h: O'Neill is back on drums for Move Back Home
years.p: He recovers and returns for the album.

years.h: Surf Goddess gets King and Livermore the fuller sound
years.p: After the stripped-down Beat Off, the EP has richer arrangements, and Dan Vapid returns on guitar.

years.h: Don't Back Down is the last Lookout! record of the decade
years.p: King, B-Face and O'Neill make it together, with J.J. Rassler back on guitar.

years.h: King wants Epitaph's three-album offer; B-Face and O'Neill don't
years.p: King replaces both with Dave Swain, from Jon Cougar Concentration Camp, and Chris Fields of the Dwarves.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, King favored the deal while his bandmates opposed it. B-Face goes on to Chixdiggit!, the Mopes and the Groovie Ghoulies.

eras.title: Joe and whoever's in the van
eras.text: King is the only fixed point as bassists and drummers rotate. O'Neill dies, labels change, and the Lookout! years end in a royalties fight.

years.h: Punk Rock Confidential is Dave Swain's first record on bass
years.p: Swain plays bass on the 1998 album and stays until 2002.

years.h: Hugh O'Neill dies of brain cancer at 41
years.p: The drummer on Love Songs for the Retarded dies January 20, 1999. King later said O'Neill was dying while Livermore was selling Lookout!.

years.h: King and Swain make Beyond the Valley...
years.p: Swain is on bass in a lineup that keeps shifting around King, the only member since 1981.

years.h: The Queers leave Lookout! for Hopeless, then return for Pleasant Screams
years.p: King tells Razorcake how he describes his relationship with labels.
years.xp:
In the interview King said Hopeless sold more records but made them less money, and that Lookout "didn't seem like they wanted us." He added that the band is "known as a Lookout! band."

He was also planning an autobiography, tentatively titled Get Out of the Van, inspired by Henry Rollins' memoir.

years.h: After six Lookout! albums, the band takes its masters back
years.p: The Queers allege breach of contract over unpaid royalties.
years.xp: The reclaimed masters allow remixed reissues of records like Love Songs for the Retarded and Beat Off on Asian Man Records in 2007.

eras.title: Still Joe Queer
eras.text: On Asian Man Records the band keeps recording and touring, with a rotating cast and King the only constant.

years.h: Munki Brain opens the Asian Man Records years
years.p: It's the first new album after the masters fight. Their "Wipe Out" cover is in the film Surf's Up the same year.

years.h: Dave Swain is back on bass
years.p: He stays until 2015.

years.h: Dwarves and Screeching Weasel line up for God Save the Queers
years.p: The tribute album also has Teengenerate and New Bomb Turks covering the band.

years.cap: The Queers on the Back to the Basement tour, c. 2010
years.h: Twenty-nine years after Tulu's basement, Back to the Basement
years.p: King and Swain are the core of the band that makes it.

years.cap: The Queers at Ruhrpott Rodeo, Germany
years.h: King's Ferguson posts draw a call to drop the band
years.p: King posts support for Darren Wilson, the officer who shot Michael Brown. Don Giovanni's Joe Steinhardt asks Asian Man and Recess to drop the Queers.
years.xp: King's reply, per Wikipedia: he called Steinhardt a "gutless wimp" and challenged him to a filmed debate.

years.cap: The Queers at One Centre Square, Easton, Pennsylvania
years.h: Save the World arrives with King still out front
years.p: King is still the only constant 39 years in, with drummer Alex Martin, who joined in 2011.

years.h: Reverberation is the latest album on the list
years.p: Forty years after the first rehearsal, King puts out another record.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Love Songs for the Retarded
